transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—I'm Dr. Lee. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Dr. Lee. Well, I guess what brings me in is... I keep getting these flashes. They just hit me completely out of nowhere. 

It's like I'm right back in that crowded holding room, seeing the fight happen all over again and hearing everybody get shoved up against the wall. It's just really intense. Like, I'll just be standing at a pickup counter for work, waiting on a package, and suddenly I'm right back there in that room.
Can you tell me how long ago that incident in the holding room happened, and how long you've been experiencing these flashbacks since then?

It's been going on for about a week now. I was detained overnight last week, and... well, that's when I saw that assault happen in the holding area. So, yeah, I've been getting these flashes pretty much ever since then.
Have you noticed yourself avoiding certain places, people, or situations that remind you of that night in the holding room?

Yeah, I have. Um, for work, I've actually been turning down all my night runs. And even during the day, I've been taking the long way around town on my routes because... well, I just can't make myself go anywhere near that detention building. 

I've also been avoiding talking about what happened with anyone. If I try to talk about it, or if I get too close to that part of town, I just start feeling like I'm right back in that room.
Since that night, have you noticed any changes in your sleep, like trouble falling or staying asleep, or feeling unusually on edge or easily startled?

Yeah, my sleep has been really bad. I barely sleep at all now. I'll maybe doze off for an hour or two, but then I'm right back up. It's usually from some dream about being in that cell, or... or just waking up in a panic because I thought I heard a door slamming. By the time morning comes around, I just feel completely wrecked. Honestly, I've been too exhausted to even drive my route safely.

Since the incident, have you had moments where you felt detached from yourself or your surroundings, like you were in a daze, watching things happen from outside your body, or like things around you weren't quite real?

No, I don't think so. I haven't really experienced anything like that. I mean, I feel pretty normal as far as... you know, being in my own body goes. Things around me feel real enough. I'm just incredibly tired and on edge all the time, but I haven't had any of those out-of-body moments or felt like I was in a daze like that.
Since the incident, have you noticed yourself feeling more irritable or having outbursts of anger that are out of character for you?

Yeah, actually. My temper has just been snapping for no reason lately. Like, the other day I completely blew up at dispatch over a minor schedule change. And then... I went to play basketball and ended up cursing out a guy just for bumping into me. Normally, I'd just shake that kind of thing off, but right now it's like I just have zero patience.
Since the incident, have you noticed yourself feeling constantly on guard or overly watchful of your surroundings, even in situations that used to feel safe?

No, I wouldn't say I'm constantly on guard or anything like that. I mean, I'm jumpy if I hear a loud noise, like I said before, but I'm not looking over my shoulder everywhere I go. When I'm at home or just out running errands, I feel safe enough. It's not like I'm watching everyone around me waiting for something bad to happen.

When something reminds you of that night—like passing near the detention building or hearing a loud noise—do you notice physical reactions such as your heart racing, sweating, or trouble catching your breath?

No, not really. I mean, I don't get sweaty or feel like I can't breathe or anything. Like I said, I definitely get jumpy with loud noises, but my heart doesn't start pounding out of my chest or anything like that. It's more just... being startled, I guess. I haven't noticed any major physical stuff like you're describing when I get reminded of it.
